---
# A starting point for EPISODIC_MAIL_TEMPLATE_REPORT: the body of the email
# a scheduled outbreak report is attached to. Copy it, adapt it, and point
# the environment variable at your copy; preview it with
# episodic_mail_template_preview("report", template_path = "...").
#
# This one keeps EpiSODIC's own message (d$default_content: the subject as
# a heading, what the report is about, how many cases are new, and when
# the next one follows) and places it inside a letterhead and signature of
# your own. Every style is inline and taken from d$mail_style, built from
# the instance palette; see the new-clusters template for why an email
# needs `minimal: true` and carries no images.
pagetitle: "EpiSODIC"
format:
  html:
    minimal: true
    embed-resources: true
params:
  data_path: "mail_data.rds"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
d <- readRDS(params$data_path)
s <- d$mail_style
esc <- function(x) EpiSODIC:::episodic_html_escape(x)
at <- function(css) EpiSODIC:::episodic_mail_style_attr(css)
```

```{r body, results='asis'}
cat(
  "```{=html}\n",
  "<div", at(s$body), ">",
  # Your organisation's letterhead goes here.
  d$default_content,
  # And your signature here. d$attachment_name is the attached file's name.
  "<p", at(s$muted), ">", esc(d$attachment_name), " &middot; EpiSODIC ",
  esc(d$package_version), "</p>",
  "</div>\n",
  "```\n",
  sep = ""
)
```
